files.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm release:check
      - run: pnpm release:check:shiso
      - run: pnpm build
      - run: pnpm test:multi-scope
      - run: pnpm test:create-app

  # The generator smoke build must pass on every supported Node version
  # (engines: ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0).
  node-support:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version: ['20.19', '22', '24']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm build
      - run: pnpm test:multi-scope
      - run: pnpm test:create-app

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Demo API
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.demo.dev/v1
security:
  - bearerAuth: []
tags:
  - name: Users
  - name: Orders
paths:
  /users:
    get:
      operationId: listUsers
      tags: [Users]
      summary: List users
      description: Returns a paginated list of users.
      security: []
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          required: true
          description: Maximum number of results.
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
        - name: offset
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A list of users.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'
    post:
      operationId: createUser
      tags: [Users]
      summary: Create a user
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/NewUser'
      responses:
        '201':
          description: The created user.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'
        '422':
          description: Validation failed.
  /users/{id}:
    parameters:
      - name: id
        in: path
        required: true
        description: User identifier.
        schema:
          type: string
          format: uuid
    get:
      operationId: getUser
      tags: [Users]
      summary: Get a user
      parameters:
        - name: X-Request-Id
          in: header
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The requested user.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'
              example:
                id: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
                name: Ada Lovelace
        '404':
          description: No user with this ID exists.
    delete:
      operationId: deleteUser
      tags: [Users]
      summary: Delete a user
      deprecated: true
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted.
  /orders:
    get:
      operationId: listOrders
      tags: [Orders]
      summary: List orders
      parameters:
        - name: status
          in: query
          description: Filter by order status.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [pending, shipped, delivered]
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A list of orders.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
  schemas:
    User:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
          description: Display name.
        email:
          type: string
          format: email
          nullable: true
        friends:
          type: array
          description: Other users this user follows.
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'
    NewUser:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          example: Ada Lovelace
        email:
          type: string
          format: email
    Order:
      type: object
      required: [id, status, payment]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, shipped, delivered]
        payment:
          oneOf:
            - $ref: '#/components/schemas/CardPayment'
            - $ref: '#/components/schemas/BankPayment'
    CardPayment:
      type: object
      properties:
        brand:
          type: string
        last4:
          type: string
    BankPayment:
      type: object
      properties:
        iban:
          type: string

---
title: Installation
description: Create a standalone Shiso documentation site with create-shiso-app.
---

Use `create-shiso-app` to start a new Shiso site. The generator creates a small
project that installs the upgradeable `@umami/shiso` framework dependency.

## Create a project

Choose the command for your package manager:

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash pnpm
  pnpm dlx create-shiso-app@latest my-docs
  ```

  ```bash npm
  npm create shiso-app@latest my-docs
  ```

  ```bash yarn
  yarn create shiso-app@latest my-docs
  ```

  ```bash bun
  bunx create-shiso-app@latest my-docs
  ```
</CodeGroup>

Replace `my-docs` with your project directory. The directory must be empty if
it already exists.

The generator:

- Copies a minimal Shiso starter site
- Installs Shiso as a regular project dependency
- Sets the package name from the project directory
- Installs dependencies with the package manager that invoked it
- Initializes a fresh Git repository on the `main` branch
- Adds no Git remote, so the project is not tied to the Shiso repository

## Start the site

Move into the generated project and start the development server:

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash pnpm
  cd my-docs
  pnpm dev
  ```

  ```bash npm
  cd my-docs
  npm run dev
  ```

  ```bash yarn
  cd my-docs
  yarn dev
  ```

  ```bash bun
  cd my-docs
  bun run dev
  ```
</CodeGroup>

Open the local URL shown in your terminal. Edit
`content/docs/index.mdx` to change the first page and `docs.json` to configure
the site and navigation.

## Upgrade Shiso

The generator is only used to create the project. Upgrade the framework later
through your package manager:

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash pnpm
  pnpm update @umami/shiso
  ```

  ```bash npm
  npm update @umami/shiso
  ```

  ```bash yarn
  yarn upgrade @umami/shiso
  ```

  ```bash bun
  bun update @umami/shiso
  ```
</CodeGroup>

This installs the newest version allowed by the range in `package.json`. When
the range does not allow the newest release, update the dependency explicitly
(e.g. `pnpm add @umami/shiso@latest`), then run `pnpm check` and `pnpm build`
to verify the upgrade.

Your content, `docs.json`, `styles.css`, and files under `public` remain in your
project; rendering and build internals update with the dependency.

## CLI options

Run `create-shiso-app --help` to see every option.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--use-pnpm` | Install dependencies with pnpm. |
| `--use-npm` | Install dependencies with npm. |
| `--use-yarn` | Install dependencies with Yarn. |
| `--use-bun` | Install dependencies with Bun. |
| `--skip-install` | Create the project without installing dependencies. |
| `--disable-git` | Create the project without initializing Git. |
| `--help` | Print command usage and options. |

## Next step

Continue to [Configuration](/docs/configuration) to customize `docs.json`, or
[Writing content](/docs/writing-content) to add pages and components.

---
title: Search and AI
description: Built-in search, markdown export, and the AI contextual menu.
---

## Search

Every Shiso site ships with client-side search — no service or API key
required. Open it with the header button or <kbd>⌘K</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl K</kbd>.

The index is built at compile time from your content: each page is split into
heading-bounded sections, so results land on the exact section that matched.
Pages marked `hidden` in navigation stay out of the index.

Customize the input placeholder and shortcut with `search.prompt`,
`search.shortcut`, and `search.shortcutLabel`. Set `shortcut` to `false` to
disable only the shortcut, or set `search` to `false` to remove search:

```json
{
  "search": {
    "prompt": "Search the docs...",
    "shortcut": "k",
    "shortcutLabel": "Ctrl K"
  }
}
```

### Search position

By default the search control sits on the right side of the header. Move it
with `search.position`:

- `header` (default) — right side of the header.
- `sidebar` — top of the navigation column. On small screens, where the
  sidebar collapses into a menu, it stays in the header.

```json
{
  "search": {
    "position": "sidebar"
  }
}
```

Positions are named slots rather than layout coordinates, so themes decide
how each one looks. Every theme supports `header`; if a theme doesn't
implement the position you asked for, search falls back to the header.

To hide the search control and disable its shortcut on one page, set
`search: false` in that page's frontmatter:

```mdx
---
title: Welcome
search: false
---
```

### Search providers

The built-in `local` provider is used by default. Shiso also ships a built-in
[Pagefind](https://pagefind.app) provider, and you can register your own.
Select a provider with `search.provider`; `options` are passed directly to its
factory:

```json
{
  "search": {
    "prompt": "Search the docs...",
    "provider": "hosted",
    "options": { "index": "docs" }
  }
}
```

### Pagefind

[Pagefind](https://pagefind.app) indexes the prerendered HTML during
`shiso build`, giving better relevance ranking, stemming, and multi-language
support than the local index — still fully static, with no service required.

Install the `pagefind` package (an optional dependency of `@umami/shiso`) and
select the provider:

```shell
pnpm add -D pagefind
```

```json
{
  "search": {
    "provider": "pagefind"
  }
}
```

`shiso build` then writes the search bundle to `dist/client/pagefind/`. In
`shiso dev` there is no prerendered HTML to index, so search transparently
falls back to the local provider until you build.

Supported `options`:

- `ranking`: passed to Pagefind's runtime
  [ranking options](https://pagefind.app/docs/ranking/), e.g.
  `{ "termFrequency": 0.8 }`
- `excludeSelectors`: CSS selectors to exclude from indexing, e.g.
  `[".changelog-date"]` (heading permalink anchors are always excluded)

Hidden pages and scopes are excluded from the index, and on multi-version or
multi-language sites results stay inside the version and language being
browsed, matching the local provider's behavior.

### Custom providers

Register custom providers in `entry-client.tsx` before hydrating Shiso:

```tsx
import { ShisoApp } from '@umami/shiso/client';
import { hydrateRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { registerSearchProvider } from '@umami/shiso/search';

registerSearchProvider('hosted', options => ({
  async search(query, limit = 10) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ q: query, limit: String(limit) });
    const response = await fetch('/api/search?' + params);

    return response.json();
  },
}));

const element = document.getElementById('root');

if (!element) {
  throw new Error('Shiso could not find the root element.');
}

hydrateRoot(element, <ShisoApp />);
```

Every provider returns normalized results with `url`, `page`, `score`, and
optional `heading` and `snippet` fields. Snippets may wrap matched terms in
`<mark>` tags, which the search dialog renders as highlights (snippets are
parsed, never injected as HTML). Provider options are included in the
browser bundle, so do not put private API keys in them. An unknown provider id
logs a warning and falls back to `local`.

## Markdown export

The production build publishes the raw markdown of every page next to its HTML:

```text
/docs/installation      the rendered page
/docs/installation.md   the markdown source
```

This powers the contextual menu below and gives AI tools a clean,
token-efficient version of every page.

### AI discovery files

Every production build also writes two site-level discovery files:

- `/llms.txt` lists navigable pages in documentation order with their titles,
  descriptions, and Markdown URLs.
- `/llms-full.txt` combines that public Markdown corpus into one file.

Pages marked `noindex`, and hidden pages or scopes under the default
`navigable` indexing policy, are omitted. Set `seo.indexing` to `all` to include
hidden documentation pages.

## Contextual menu

The `contextual` key adds a menu beside the page title for AI-optimized
actions. The first option is the primary button; the rest go in a dropdown.

```json
{
  "contextual": {
    "options": ["copy", "view", "chatgpt", "claude", "perplexity"]
  }
}
```

- `copy`: copy the page as Markdown to the clipboard
- `view`: open the page's markdown source in a new tab
- `chatgpt`, `claude`, `perplexity`: open the assistant with a prompt pointing
  at the page's markdown URL (requires
  [`siteUrl`](/docs/project-settings#production-site-url) in `shiso.config.ts`)

### Custom options

Define your own entries as objects. `$path` expands to the page path and
`$page` to the page's markdown URL:

```json
{
  "contextual": {
    "options": [
      "copy",
      {
        "title": "Ask support",
        "description": "Send this page to the support bot",
        "icon": "life-buoy",
        "href": "https://example.com/ask?page=$path",
        "target": "_blank"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Custom options render the configured icon and infer `_self` for local links
and `_blank` for external links unless `target` overrides it.

---
title: API references
description: Generate API reference pages from an OpenAPI spec.
---

Shiso turns a local OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 spec (JSON or YAML) into full reference
pages: parameters, request and response schemas, status codes, ready-to-use
code samples in cURL, JavaScript, and Python, and an interactive "Try it"
panel that sends real requests from the browser. Everything is resolved at
build time — no client-side spec parsing and no external service.

See the [API demo](/docs/api-reference/list-users) section in this site's
Documentation tab for a live example.

## Point at your spec

Add the `api` key to `docs.json`:

```json
{
  "api": {
    "spec": "openapi.yaml",
    "directory": "api-reference"
  }
}
```

- `spec`: path to the spec file, relative to the project root, or an `https`
  URL. A list of specs is accepted too; see [Multiple specs](#multiple-specs).
- `directory` (optional): folder inside your content directory where endpoint
  pages live. Defaults to `api-reference`.

### Hosted specs

Point `spec` at a URL to document an API whose spec is published elsewhere:

```json
{
  "api": {
    "spec": "https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  }
}
```

The document is downloaded whenever the configuration loads and cached under
`.shiso/openapi-cache`, so a build still succeeds when the URL is temporarily
unreachable (a warning notes that the cached copy was used). Commit the cache
directory if you need fully offline builds.

### Multiple specs

List several specs to document more than one API on the same site:

```json
{
  "api": {
    "spec": ["specs/users.yaml", "https://billing.example.com/openapi.json"],
    "directory": "api-reference"
  }
}
```

Each spec's endpoint pages land in their own subfolder named after the spec
file (`api-reference/users/…`, `api-reference/openapi/…`). Operations and
schemas are looked up by their bare key (`GET /users`, `User`) when only one
spec defines them; when several do, qualify the key with the spec as
configured — `openapi: specs/users.yaml GET /users` — or `pnpm check` reports
the ambiguity. Generated stubs on multi-spec sites always use the qualified
form.

## Add endpoints to navigation

Use an `openapi` entry anywhere a page list is accepted:

```json
{
  "navigation": {
    "groups": [
      { "group": "API reference", "pages": [{ "openapi": true }] },
      { "group": "Users API", "pages": [{ "openapi": "Users API" }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `{ "openapi": true }` expands into one group per spec tag, containing every
  operation. Webhooks without tags collect in a "Webhooks" group.
- `{ "openapi": "<tag>" }` expands into a flat list of that tag's operations.
- `{ "openapi": "<spec>" }`, where `<spec>` is a path or URL from `api.spec`,
  expands into that spec's tag groups on multi-spec sites.

Expanded entries show a colored method badge (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE,
or HOOK for webhooks) next to the page title in the sidebar.

## Endpoint pages

For every operation, Shiso creates a stub page in the configured directory the
first time the config loads:

```mdx
---
title: "Get a user"
openapi: GET /users/{id}
---
```

The `openapi` frontmatter key binds the page to an operation by method and
path. The page then renders the operation's summary badge, parameters, request
body, responses, and code samples below any prose you write in the body.

Commit the stub files: they are ordinary content pages, which keeps search,
markdown export, and navigation working exactly like the rest of your docs.
Existing files are never overwritten, so you can freely edit titles, add
descriptions, or write an introduction above the generated reference.

## Webhooks

Entries under the spec's top-level `webhooks` map (OpenAPI 3.1) or the
`x-webhooks` extension (OpenAPI 3.0) become pages too. Bind one with
`openapi: webhook <name>`:

```mdx
---
title: "User created"
openapi: webhook user.created
---
```

A webhook page shows a WEBHOOK badge, the **Payload** the API sends, and the
responses it expects back. Webhooks describe requests your API makes, so they
have no code samples and no playground.

## Schema pages

Document a named schema from `components.schemas` on its own page with the
`openapi-schema` frontmatter key:

```mdx
---
title: "User object"
description: "The user record returned by every user endpoint."
openapi-schema: User
---

Any prose you write here appears above the generated reference.
```

The page renders the schema's **Properties** table (nested objects expand in
place) and a highlighted **Example**, taken from the spec or derived from the
schema. Schema pages are ordinary content pages: add them to `navigation`,
and they are searchable and exported as Markdown like every other page. See
the [User object](/docs/api-reference/user) page in this site's API demo.

When both `openapi` and `openapi-schema` resolve on the same page, the
operation reference takes precedence. Rendering, search, link validation,
and Markdown export all use its sections. Invalid bindings are still reported
by the content checker.

## What gets generated

- **Try it** — the interactive playground described below.
- **Parameters** — path, query, header, and cookie parameters rendered as
  fields. Each security scheme the operation accepts adds an entry where the
  credential is sent: `Authorization` for HTTP bearer and basic schemes, and
  the configured header, query, or cookie name for API keys.
- **Request body** — the schema tree with nested and expandable object
  properties, plus a highlighted example (taken from the spec, or derived from
  the schema when the spec has none).
- **Responses** — one entry per status code with schema and example.
- **Code samples** — cURL, JavaScript `fetch`, and Python `requests` snippets
  built from the operation, highlighted with the same theme as your
  [code blocks](/docs/customization#code-blocks). Samples send credentials the
  way the spec declares them, use the operation's own `servers` entry when it
  has one, and encode JSON, form-urlencoded, multipart, and raw bodies
  according to the request body's content type.

## API playground

Every endpoint page opens with a **Try it** panel: a form built from the
operation's servers, security schemes, parameters, and request body. Send
request runs the call from the browser and shows the status, timing, response
headers, and a pretty-printed body. A collapsible **Request** section shows the
exact cURL command for the current inputs, so readers can copy it to a
terminal instead.

- The **Server** field starts at the operation's first server URL. When the
  spec lists several servers, they appear as suggestions; any URL can be typed,
  which is handy for pointing the playground at a local instance.
- **Authorization** shows one input per security scheme: a token for bearer
  and OAuth schemes, a username and password for HTTP basic, and a key for
  `apiKey` schemes. Values are kept in the browser tab's session storage so
  they are reused across endpoint pages and cleared when the tab closes.
- Parameters are prefilled with the spec's examples or defaults. Enum and
  boolean parameters render as selects. Cookie parameters cannot be set from
  browser scripts and are listed for reference only.
- The **Body** editor is prefilled with the example request. For
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data` operations,
  enter a JSON object; its keys become form fields.

Requests are sent with `fetch` directly from the reader's browser, so the API
must allow cross-origin requests from your docs domain. When it does not,
route requests through a proxy you host:

```json
{
  "api": {
    "spec": "openapi.yaml",
    "playground": {
      "proxy": "https://proxy.example.com/?url=$url"
    }
  }
}
```

`$url` is replaced with the URL-encoded target; if the value has no `$url`,
the encoded target is appended to it. Shiso does not ship a proxy: any CORS
proxy that forwards the method, headers, and body will do.

### Turn the playground off

Set `api.playground.display` to `"simple"` or `"none"` to render endpoint
pages without the panel (both values are accepted for compatibility with
Mintlify configs and behave the same):

```json
{
  "api": {
    "spec": "openapi.yaml",
    "playground": { "display": "none" }
  }
}
```

Override the site setting on one page with `playground` frontmatter:

```mdx
---
title: "Delete a user"
openapi: DELETE /users/{id}
playground: none
---
```

The published Markdown copy of each endpoint page (used by the contextual menu
and `llms-full.txt`) includes a Markdown rendering of the full reference.

## Notes and limitations

- `$ref` references must point inside the spec document; remote or file
  references are not resolved.
- Server URL variables are filled with their `default` values. Relative server
  URLs (such as `/v1`) are used as written, so type a full URL in the
  playground's Server field to call them.
- Recursive schemas render as their type name once a cycle is detected.
- Swagger 2.0 specs are not supported — convert them to OpenAPI 3 first.
- Avoid headings named "Try it", "Headers", "Path parameters", "Query
  parameters", "Cookie parameters", "Request body", "Payload", "Responses", or
  "Code samples" in an endpoint page's prose, and "Properties" or "Example" on
  a schema page; the generated sections already use those anchors.
- In `shiso dev`, editing the spec regenerates stubs for new operations and
  reloads the site. Removing an operation leaves its stub behind — delete the
  file and its navigation reference manually if you no longer want the page.

title: Deployment
description: Ship the static build to any host.
---

`pnpm build` produces a fully static site in `dist/client` — plain HTML, CSS,
and JavaScript with no server component. Any static host works.

The output includes:

- a prerendered `index.html` for every page
- `sitemap.xml` (when [`siteUrl`](/docs/project-settings#production-site-url) is set)
- redirect pages for every [`redirects`](/docs/seo#redirects) rule
- a `.md` copy of every page for [AI tools](/docs/search-and-ai#markdown-export)
- `404.html` for hosts that serve it on unknown paths

## GitHub Pages

Point Pages at the build output with an action:

```yaml
name: Deploy docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for last-modified timestamps
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist/client
      - uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

GitHub Pages serves `404.html` for unknown paths automatically, so client-side
routing keeps working on deep links.

## Netlify

- **Build command**: `pnpm build`
- **Publish directory**: `dist/client`

## Vercel

The repository includes `vercel.json`, which configures:

- **Build command**: `pnpm build`
- **Framework preset**: `Other`
- **Output directory**: `dist/client`

Shiso prerenders its own routes, so Vercel serves it as a static site rather
than applying generic Vite SPA routing. The output-directory override ensures
Vercel serves the site nested in `dist/client`.

## Cloudflare Pages

- **Build command**: `pnpm build`
- **Build output directory**: `dist/client`

## Deploying under a subpath

When the site lives at `https://example.com/my-docs/` rather than a domain
root, pass the base path to `shiso build`:

```json
{
  "build": "shiso build --base=/my-docs/"
}
```

The prerenderer detects the base from the build output and lays out the
directories to match.

## Checklist

1. Set [`siteUrl`](/docs/project-settings#production-site-url) in
   `shiso.config.ts` so canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, and the sitemap
   are emitted.
2. Use a full-history checkout (`fetch-depth: 0`) if
   [`metadata.timestamp`](/docs/seo#last-modified-timestamps) is enabled.
3. Verify a deep link (any docs page URL) after the first deploy.
